rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses cyclic/high-strain-rate mechanical loading to induce phase separation, while the target uses thermal aging at specific temperatures to control ordering and phase boundary evolution. These are fundamentally different kinds of intervention (mechanical vs. thermal).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high strain rates and service-relevant temperatures near operational limits, while the target uses a specific thermal aging window (550-750°C) without mechanical loading. The regimes differ entirely.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes strain-induced nano-scale phase separation creating brittle precipitates, whereas the target describes enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, and stress concentration at jagged phase boundaries. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced toughness and brittle fracture under mechanical loading, while the target predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with temperature-dependent ductility recovery. The predicted property direction and pattern differ.
